cohort: Sixty parturients receiving epidural labour analgesia at two tertiary care hospitals were divided into two equal groups.
finding: Ropivacaine had a significantly faster onset of analgesia and better early pain relief, while levobupivacaine offered a significantly longer duration of analgesia; both agents showed comparable maternal and fetal safety profiles.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was comparable and not statistically different between the ropivacaine and levobupivacaine groups.
birth_weight: Measured as a fetal outcome, but specific weights or range were not provided.
